title: Augmented strict-poset chains with alternating deletion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ a partially ordered set. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ let $B_n(P)$ consist of lists $l$ of elements of $P$ satisfying $l_a<l_b$ whenever $a<b$ and $|l|=n+1$. Define $C_n(P;R)=\{a:B_n(P)\to R\mid a\text{ has finite support}\}$, with pointwise module operations. For any list $l$, write $[l]_n$ for its unit basis vector if $l\in B_n(P)$, and zero otherwise; in particular repeated weakly increasing lists denote zero. Thus $B_{-1}(P)$ has the unique empty list, $C_{-1}(P;R)$ is canonically $R$ on $[\varnothing]$, and $C_n(P;R)=0$ for $n<-1$. Define $d_{ij}$ to be zero unless $i=j+1$, and in that case extend the rule $d_{ij}[l]_i=\sum_{a=0}^{|l|-1}(-1)^a[l\text{ with vertex }a\text{ deleted}]_j$ linearly. Let $C(P;R)$ be the integer-indexed chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] with these terms and differentials; the chain-complex proof obligation is the cancellation of each double deletion in the two possible orders. In particular a vertex maps to the empty generator and the empty generator has zero differential.
